functions.name: mlk_poly_add
functions.role: In-place coefficient-wise addition of polynomial b into polynomial r without modular reduction inside the function body; intended repository counterpart of ML-KEM polynomial addition used in K-PKE.Encrypt before later reduction.
inputs: r: pointer to mutable mlk_poly whose coeffs array is updated in place
b: pointer to const mlk_poly whose coeffs array is read
outputs: Post-state r->coeffs[k] equals old r->coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k] for all k in 0..MLKEM_N-1, under stated preconditions
modified_memory: memory slice of *r only; b is read-only

evidence_references.excerpt: void mlk_poly_add(mlk_poly *r, const mlk_poly *b) __contract__( requires(memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(forall(k0, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] + b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX)) requires(forall(k1, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] + b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN)) ensures(forall(k, 0, MLKEM_N, r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k])) assigns(memory_slice(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) );
evidence_references.supports_claim: Signature, preconditions, postcondition, and write-set of mlk_poly_add.

evidence_references.excerpt: for (i = 0; i < MLKEM_N; i++) ... { /* The preconditions imply that the addition stays within int16_t. */ r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i]); }
evidence_references.supports_claim: Implementation performs element-wise in-place addition over all coefficients with explicit int16_t cast.

evidence_references.excerpt: We use destructive version (output=first input) to avoid reasoning about aliasing in the CBMC specification
evidence_references.supports_claim: Function is intentionally destructive/in-place and the design motivation is aliasing simplification for specification/proof work.

evidence_references.supports_claim: Repository comment links mlk_poly_add to FIPS polynomial addition and a use site in K-PKE.Encrypt.

evidence_references.excerpt: The algebraic operations of addition and scalar multiplication in R_q and T_q are done coordinate-wise... performed by addition ... of the corresponding coefficient arrays.
evidence_references.supports_claim: Cautious traceability basis that coefficient-wise array addition is the specification-level operation that this implementation appears intended to correspond to.

functions.uncertainty: The code-level operation is exact machine-integer addition under int16_t-range assumptions, not an explicit modular reduction. Equivalence to exact Z_q output requires later reasoning about surrounding calls such as mlk_poly_reduce.
limitations: No explicit runtime check enforces the int16_t no-overflow assumptions in non-CBMC/non-debug builds; they are contractual preconditions.
The function does not itself guarantee canonical 0..q-1 output coefficients.

If callers violate non-aliasing freshness-style assumptions used by contracts, later proof obligations may fail even though some concrete aliasing patterns such as r==b may still produce defined arithmetic results.
